title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.1 & 2.2 Report, Modeling Myanmar's path to a Near-Zero Emissions Power sector by 2050

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Myanmar-specific pathway following current energy policies and NDCs.
pathwayDescription: The Existing Policies Pathway (EPP) is a predictive power-sector scenario for Myanmar modeling the energy system under current policies and Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) targets. It is complemented by two pathways from the same developers: the Optimized Existing Policy Pathway, which uses the same assumptions with cost optimization, and the Optimized More Ambitious Pathway, which reaches near-zero power-sector emissions by 2050. EPP projects demand growth across all major sectors and reflects planned gas, hydro, and solar additions alongside retirements of aging thermal assets. Renewables expand moderately; no major policy shifts or large-scale low-carbon interventions are assumed. Reserve margins tighten as demand grows and new firm capacity remains limited. Generation rises 57% from 2020 to 2040, then falls 16% by 2050, causing a domestic supply shortfall. Direct emissions fall as coal and gas are phased out by 2050, though imports reaching 14% of demand may offset this.

energyEfficiency.value: Not applicable at this scope level

coreDrivers.policies: Demand side sector energy demand follows Myanmar official targets. To fulffil those additional demands, the scenario follows Myanmar official technology shares targets in 2030, sourced from a World Bank report. Myanmar also issued NDC Capacity targets additions, but due to political instability, challenges with natural gas supply, and the lack of foreign investment, the country power development landscape has changed.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Follows SSP2. GDP and medium population growth extracted from World Bank data, sectoral value-added trends are modeled based on historic World Bank data. These all drive electricity demand.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Aging-plant retirements and supply constraints are a dominant driver. It leads to a shrtage in supply in the power sector.

dependencies.dependency_description: National targets shapes power generation demand. An additional renewables technology share target is added in 2030. Myanmar also issued NDC Capacity targets additions, but due to political instability, challenges with natural gas supply, and the lack of foreign investment, the country power development landscape has changed, and those capacity additions are not the most likely to happen.
Renewables capacity expansion is aligned with policies but is unsufficient to meet demand due to gas power plant retirement. Significant electricty import would be necessary to supply demand.
Local opposition to large hydropower already stricked in Myanmar. This scenario significantly rely on hydro expansion.
Consumer and client are assumed to follow Myanmar power demand target.

EPP's reserve margin falls to -51% due to inadequate replacement capacity. This negative reserve margin indicates a significant shortage of available capacity to meet peak demand, increasing the risk of frequent power shortages nationwide.
EPP significantly depends on hydropower and imports after gas retirements. Hydropower availability may be reduced over time due to more severe droughts and changes in rain patterns.
Drought and climate variability threaten hydropower reliability.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Emissions intensity can be derived from total generation and absolute emissions. Covers domestic generation only; imported-electricity emissions, significant in EP, are excluded. As fossil power is phased out domestically, intensity tends to 0.
